title: Fit lever-lock chain handcuffs on two training wrist forms: each bar ratcheted to a fingertip gap, then double-locked
instruction: Put one handcuff round each wrist form. Close each cuff so a 6 mm rod still fits between cuff and form but a 12 mm rod does not. Double-lock both cuffs. Then move both grippers clear.
context: Handcuffing is regular core work for two large occupations: police and sheriff's patrol officers (646,310 employed, BLS OEWS May 2023, https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/may/oes333051.htm) and correctional officers and jailers (351,420, https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/may/oes333012.htm), 997,730 together. Patrol officers cuff at arrests and before transport; correctional officers restrain people for escorts, transfers and cell moves, many times a shift. Training rules ask for a fingertip of room and an immediate double lock, because a cuff that keeps tightening can injure the wrist nerve, and the ratchet cannot be backed out without the key. Unlike fastening a clasp or bracelet, where the part snaps shut at one fixed position, each cuff here is a one-way ratchet that must be stopped at a gauged fit, neither loose nor over-tight, and then frozen with a second lock, on two chained cuffs with both arms. This is a bench drill on rigid forms; no person is involved.
setup: Two YAM arms with parallel grippers at the near edge of the table, and a fixed camera above the table looking down. Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm on the table top. Two wrist forms, hard plastic, fixed to the table: an upright post with a stadium outline (54 x 40 mm, round ends), 30 mm tall, long side along x, topped by a 70 x 36 x 10 mm flat stadium cap that stands in for the hand. Near form centre at (12.0, 5.0), far form at (29.2, 5.0). One pair of nickel-plated steel chain handcuffs sized on the Smith & Wesson Model 100 lever-lock (328 g pair in the model). Each cuff has: a fixed double bar (8 mm wide, 10 mm thick over both cheeks) from the hinge rivet round to the lock case; a lock case 34 x 33.5 x 13 mm whose end is 104 mm from the rivet; a swinging single bar (6.4 mm wide, 4 mm thick) hinged at the rivet, with 23 locking positions 3.0 mm apart at the teeth (2.15 degrees each); a yellow double-lock lever tab (5.5 x 10 x 8 mm) on the end of the lock case, which slides 5.5 mm across the case against a spring (2.2 N to push it home). Masses per cuff: 118 g body, 36 g bar, 4 g lever. Chain: two 6 g links, 56 mm between the swivel eyes on the lock-case ends. Start: both cuffs flat on the table, swinging bars open 95 degrees. Cuff A rivet at (8.2, -2.0), lock case toward +x. Cuff B turned over on its swivel, rivet at (32.5, 0.8), lock case toward -x. These are reference positions. Every trial draws offsets from its seed: the whole pair moves 15 to 35 mm toward -y; on top of that cuff A moves by up to 12 mm in x and 15 mm in y, cuff B independently by up to 8 mm in x and y, and each cuff turns by up to 6 degrees (anticlockwise seen from above is positive); a draw that would over-stretch the chain is drawn again. The setup image is seed 0: cuff A rivet at (8.7, -4.6) turned -0.9 degrees, cuff B rivet at (33.2, -2.2) turned -5.2 degrees. Both arms start at the same ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Tools: luggage scale, 6 mm and 12 mm gauge rods, ruler. Scored at the end with both grippers at least 50 mm from every cuff part, otherwise 0. Each wrist form scores only if exactly one cuff is round it. Per form: 0.20 latched (a 30 N pull on the swinging bar away from the lock case for 2 s backs it out less than 3 mm, one tooth, and the form is still inside the cuff); +0.15 gap (side play of the cuff on the form, taken up with 3 N each way with the form held still, is at least 6 mm and under 12 mm: the 6 mm rod passes between bar and form, the 12 mm rod does not); +0.15 double-locked (play at least 6 mm and a 20 N squeeze of the bar toward the double bar for 1 s advances it less than 3 mm). Score = sum over the two forms, 1.0 at most. So: unlatched cuffs 0; too tight 0.2 per form; too loose and double-locked 0.35 per form; right gap but not double-locked 0.35 per form.
reset_notes: Unlock both cuffs with the key, slide the lever tabs back, swing the bars open to 95 degrees and lay the cuffs at their marks, cuff B turned over. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Official yam_arena simulator (PhysX), 20 Hz control. By rule, not by contact: the ratchet (the hinge stop follows the deepest notch reached; 3.5 N at the teeth passes a tooth) and the double lock (lever past 4.8 of 5.5 mm freezes the bar). The scorer applies the 30 N pull and 20 N squeeze as rules on the notch and lever (checked once by force: 0.6 mm back-out at 30 N). Forms are rigid and fixed. Not maker data: lever shape and travel, tooth size, pawl spring, bar outline.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps); scripted demo: 1.0 on seeds 0, 1 and 2 (1,518 steps each)
